translations.source_sense_description: fachsprachlich: sich auf zwei Beinen/Füßen fortbewegend

glosses: An animal, being, or construction that goes about on two feet (or two legs).

examples.text: He was badgered in that witness-box for an hour. By a distracting repetition of cross-examination he was forced to confess that he had seen and spoken to a human biped in broad daylight, yet could not recollect one singularity to distinguish this phantom from the flat mass of humanity.

Luján, or, rather, the biped which used to be Luján, walks right up to him. He is a little shorter than Wheeler, but much heavier-set. Rooted to the spot, not thinking clearly, Wheeler holds his violin up, as if this will shield him. The conductor takes the instrument from his unresisting hands and breaks its neck underfoot, perfunctorily, as if crushing a box for recycling.

translations.source_sense_description: fachsprachlich: sich auf zwei Beinen/Füßen fortbewegend

glosses: Having two feet or two legs; biped.

examples.text: Initial reports indicate the vessel contains a large number of intelligent bipedal aliens in some form of hibernation.

translations.source_sense_description: fachsprachlich: sich auf zwei Beinen/Füßen fortbewegend

glosses: Ambidextrous of the feet; having equal ability with either foot.

examples.text: Fred Flanagan, for two-footed kicking, marking ability and instinctive leadership, has been the best of the centre half forwards, but not much ahead of "Whopper" Lane.
In contrast to his club duties, he had a role towards the left, but a change of flanks has no significance for a two-footed player.
